5. It appears from the impugned judgment that on consideration of the evidence on record learned Additional Sessions Judge constructed the following case as against the appellant: 

 7. Keeping in view the narration as above which the learned Additional Sessions Judge held to have been proved by the prosecution we consider the evidence on record. PW 1 Harun-ur-Rashid is the father of Humayun and informant of the case. He heard about the occurrence by telephone, went to Holy Family Hospital and found his son dead. PW 2 Nazma Kabir is the widow of Humayun. She stated that on hearing about the occurrence she also went to Holy Family Hospital and found her husband dead. In her cross examination she denied that her husband tried to develop intimate relation with Nayantara. PW 3 Momtazuddin is the Constable who carried the dead body to the morgue. 

 8. PW 4 Md. Jashimuddin was an employee in the office of Humayun. He is also a nephew of Humayun. He stated that he did not know about any immoral relationship between Humayun and Nayantara. PW 5 is Nayantara. We will discuss her evidence later on. PW 6 ASI Mainuddin filled up the FIR form, PW 7 Md. Nuru Mia is the owner of the rickshaw on which Humayun was assaulted. PW 8 Falu Mia is the rickshaw puller. We will discuss his evidence later on. 

 10. PW 13 is Md. Shamim Ahmed and PW 14 Jasimuddin is a friend of PW 13. We will discuss their evidence later on. PW 15 Md. Abdul Jalil Sheikh is the Magistrate who recorded the statement of PW 13 under section 164 CrPC. PW 16 Md. Shahabuddin and PW 17 Md. Abdul Jalil Sheikh are the Investigating Officers of this case. PW 18 Dr. Mohammad Mizanul Huq held autopsy on the dead body. According to him, Humayun met with homicidal death as a result of receiving a slab injury on the left side of his throat. 

 11. Now we discuss the evidence of PW 13 Shamim Ahmed, PW 14 Jasimuddin, PW 5 Nayantara and PW 8 Falu Mia serially. PW 13 deposed that Swapan told him that he had love affairs with Nayantara, that he used to write letters under the pseudonym of Mehedi Hasan, that she also used to write letters to him, that Swapan often used to come to his sister's house at Dhaka and then Swapan used to use his (PW 13) address and the telephone number of PW 14 who corroborated PW 13 in this respect. So evidence of PW 13 and PW 14 at best prove that Swapan had love-affairs with Nayantara, that Swapan often used to come to Dhaka and used to contact Nayantara by using the address of PW 13 and the telephone of PW 14. But if we accept this part of the prosecution case as narrated by PW 13 and PW 14, even then it cannot be held that Swapan must have committed the murder. The prosecution is required to establish by positive evidence that the appellant along with others committed the murder. 

 12. PW 5 Nayantara was declared hostile by the prosecution. She did not support the prosecution case of appellant having assaulted Humayun. So we are left with the evidence of PW 8 Falu Mia in whose presence prosecution alleged that Swapan assaulted Humayun. 

 13. While in the witness-box PW 8 identified Swapan as the person who stabbed Humayun, PW 8 deposed in the witness box that the assailant boxed him on his chest, then one of his companions kept him pressed with the wall nearby at dagger point and from that position he witnessed the assault. PW 8 was examined by the Investigating Officer PW 17 Abdul Jalil Sheikh. PW 17 stated in his cross-examinaion that Falu Mia stated to him that the woman (meaning Nayantara) alighted from his rickshaw from the left side and ran towards north and that he (Falu Mia) also followed her. That soon after the attack on Humayun, Nayantara and then Falu Mia ran away from the scene was the natural behavior of the two and Falu Mia stated so when he was examined by the Investigating Officer. But in the witness box it appears he made improvement, obviously at the instance of the prosecution. Falu Mia being a poor rickshaw puller is not expected to withstand the demand of the prosecution to say in the witness-box what he was dictated to say. We, therefore, hold that it was not possible for Falu Mia to recognise and remember the face of the assailant. We further hold that there is no evidence to connect appellant Swapan with the crime. 

 14. There is, no doubt, strong suspicion here and there in the evidence of the PWs. to presume that the appellant might have committed the murder. But it is well-settled that suspicion however strong is not substitute for proof. The mind is apt to take a pleasure in adapting circumstances to one another and even straining them a little to force them to form parts of one connected whole. We find from the impugned judgment that the mind of the learned Additional Sessions Judge reacted in that way and consequently he could not distinguish between the evidence and the suspicion. Thus the impugned conviction cannot be sustained.
